title: Ukraine's Winning Strategy Against Russia: Attrition
gist: RAND's Gian Gentile and Andrew Radin argue the consensus that attrition favours Russia has inverted: Ukraine has built a metric-driven attrition machine -- targeting 200 Russian dead per square kilometre lost and 50,000 Russian soldiers eliminated monthly -- backed by a domestic drone industry, indigenous command-and-control and an ePoints kill-verification incentive scheme. Combined with long-range strikes on Russian oil and gas infrastructure that cut export revenue, they see Russia's war economy going underwater, a state of emergency declared in Crimea, and real unrest inside the population and oligarchy.

insights.claim: The prevailing assumption since February 2022 -- that attrition warfare in the Russia-Ukraine conflict would undoubtedly favour Russia because of its threefold population advantage and demonstrated tolerance for huge personnel losses -- has been overturned by recent reporting and analysis.
insights.speaker: Gian Gentile
insights.so_what: A RAND-badged reversal of the base case matters for Western aid politics, Russian sovereign risk pricing and any positioning premised on a frozen or Russia-favourable outcome.
insights.quote: Ukraine is winning the war against Russia through a strategy of attrition.
insights.locator: Ukraine is winning the war against Russia

insights.claim: Russia's war economy is described as going underwater, with very real signs of unrest within parts of the population and the Russian oligarchy.
insights.speaker: Gian Gentile
insights.so_what: Elite-cohesion cracks are the leading indicator for regime-behaviour change; they matter more to commodity and sanctions pricing than territorial lines.
insights.quote: Russia's war economy is going underwater.
insights.locator: But recent reporting and analyses suggest

insights.claim: Russia's declaration of a state of emergency in Crimea in response to Ukrainian strikes against logistics supply lines is presented as evidence of an increasingly precarious Russian position.
insights.speaker: Gian Gentile
insights.so_what: Emergency declarations are observable, dateable signals of logistics degradation -- a concrete tripwire to monitor rather than a narrative claim.
insights.locator: The recent Russian declaration of emergency in Crimea

insights.claim: The analysts explicitly reject the widely argued position that Ukraine must conduct offensive operations to seize key terrain in order to force Russia to terms.
insights.speaker: Gian Gentile
insights.so_what: Reframes what counts as Ukrainian success -- absence of a visible counteroffensive should no longer be read as stalemate or failure.
insights.locator: Some have maintained that, to win

insights.claim: Ukraine's leadership applies explicit business-style key performance metrics to warfighting: former Defence Minister Mykhailo Fedorov's war plan targets 200 Russians killed for each square kilometre of territory seized and elimination of at least 50,000 Russian soldiers each month.
insights.speaker: Gian Gentile
insights.so_what: Explicit KPIs make Ukrainian performance measurable against a stated benchmark -- the cleanest available yardstick for judging whether the attrition thesis is holding.
insights.quote: make Russia suffer 200 killed for each square kilometer of territory seized and eliminate at least 50,000 Russian soldiers each month
insights.locator: The key performance metrics in former Minister of Defense Mykhailo Fedorov's war plan

insights.claim: The ePoints system incentivises Ukrainian units to submit video evidence of their kills in exchange for points redeemable for additional drones, creating a market-like feedback loop between verified battlefield output and equipment supply.
insights.speaker: Gian Gentile
insights.so_what: A performance-linked procurement mechanism is a genuine defence-tech innovation others will copy; it also generates the data layer that makes attrition efficiency improvable.

insights.claim: Fedorov's mathematics of war initiative collected data specifically to improve the efficiency of attrition, treating kill-per-resource as an optimisable variable rather than a byproduct of combat.
insights.speaker: Gian Gentile
insights.so_what: Data-driven attrition is the exportable doctrine from this war -- watch which NATO militaries and defence software vendors adopt it.

insights.claim: Ukraine's enabling capabilities are domestic rather than donated: its own drone industry, internally developed command-and-control systems, and the training and organisation of dedicated drone forces, in particular the specialised Unmanned Systems Forces.
insights.speaker: Gian Gentile
insights.so_what: Domestic industrial depth reduces Ukraine's sensitivity to aid interruptions and creates a European drone supply chain that will outlast the war.
insights.locator: Ukraine's defense sector is making these goals attainable

insights.claim: Ukraine's attrition strategy extends into Russia's interior with continued strikes on oil and gas infrastructure, whose crucial effect is reducing oil exports and thereby weakening the Russian economy's capacity to fund the war.
insights.speaker: Gian Gentile
insights.so_what: Directly links battlefield drone reach to Russian export volumes -- a persistent, non-sanctions supply risk that crude and refined-product markets have to price.
insights.locator: Ukraine's attrition strategy also extends deep into Russia's interior

insights.claim: Ukrainian long-range strikes carry deliberate propaganda value, illustrated by a hit near St Petersburg while Putin was hosting an economic conference in early June.
insights.speaker: Gian Gentile
insights.so_what: Strike timing targeted at investor-facing set pieces raises the political cost of Russian economic diplomacy and can move sentiment independently of physical damage.

insights.claim: The war's outcome is made conditional on three specific inputs: Ukraine maintaining its attrition strategy, continuing or increasing long-range strikes into Russia, and sustained support from partner nations.
insights.speaker: Gian Gentile
insights.so_what: A three-variable conditional worth monitoring directly -- any one failing invalidates the winning-through-attrition call.
insights.locator: Whether the Russian Army faces a similar fate

insights.claim: Most wars in history have been won by attrition rather than annihilation, with Union Gen. Ulysses S. Grant abandoning the West Point doctrine of a single decisive battle in favour of grinding the Confederate Army down to surrender in April 1865.
insights.speaker: Gian Gentile
insights.so_what: Reframes attrition from a dirty word into the historical base rate -- useful for discounting analyst commentary that treats slow grinding as evidence of failure.
insights.locator: Most wars in history, though, have been won by attrition

insights.claim: Destroying an adversary's army does not reliably produce a favourable political outcome: the US destroyed the Iraqi Army on the ground in spring 2003 and still spent the next eight years mired in a multi-faceted insurgency.
insights.speaker: Gian Gentile
insights.so_what: A caution against reading decisive military events as political resolution -- applies equally to any scenario involving abrupt Russian battlefield collapse.
insights.locator: In the American invasion of Iraq in the spring of 2003

insights.claim: Russian casualty tolerance dwarfs the historical American threshold that broke domestic support: around 350 US service members were killed in one week at the height of the Tet Offensive in February 1968, whereas the Russian Army is currently suffering over 300 killed in action every day with little effective domestic opposition.
insights.speaker: Gian Gentile
insights.so_what: The central bear case against the thesis: casualty rates alone will not force Putin's hand, so the trade depends on economic and elite channels instead.
insights.locator: During the Tet Offensive in February 1968

insights.claim: The 1918 precedent offers the mechanism by which Russia could still break: after four years of attritional warfare and the defeat of the German Spring Offensive, the German Army collapsed on the battlefield, leading to the November armistice.
insights.speaker: Gian Gentile
insights.so_what: Suggests an abrupt, non-linear end state rather than gradual negotiation -- a tail scenario with outsized implications for energy, European defence spending and Russian assets.
insights.locator: But Ukraine could very well break Russia's will
